name: CBRE Group

logo.source: en.wikipedia.org infobox logo (CBRE_Group.svg, hosted on commons.wikimedia.org)

description: CBRE is the world's largest commercial real estate services firm by 2025 revenue. It earns money in four very different ways. Most of its revenue (57%) is Building Operations & Experience: multi-year contracts to run buildings for corporations and owners (HVAC, janitorial, security, property management, data-center technical services), where more than half of the reported revenue is costs passed through to clients at little or no margin. Advisory Services (22% of revenue but about 48% of segment profit) is commissions and fees on leasing, property sales, mortgage origination, valuation and loan servicing. Project Management is Turner & Townsend (70% owned), fee-for-service management of construction and capital projects. Real Estate Investments manages about $155.5 billion of assets for institutions and develops property (Trammell Crow Company). CBRE pays no dividend and buys back stock.

gics.note: Conventional GICS label as listed in Wikipedia's 'List of S&P 500 companies' (GICS Sector and GICS Sub-Industry columns, read 2026-09-30). That list gives no industry group or industry column, so those are null. SEC SIC code is 6500 (Real Estate), from the EDGAR submissions record.

hq.note: 2121 North Pearl Street, Suite 300, Dallas, TX 75201 (FY2025 10-K cover); incorporated in Delaware

employees.note: 'More than 155,000 employees (including Turner & Townsend employees)' (FY2025 10-K, Item 1 Human Capital); about 61% of CBRE employees excluding Turner & Townsend are client-reimbursed, mainly in Building Operations & Experience

businessLines.name: Advisory Services
businessLines.how: Investors and occupiers pay a commission or fee when a lease, property sale or mortgage is completed (transaction-driven, so it rises and falls with deal volume), plus recurring fees for valuations and for servicing loans over their life.
businessLines.description: Leasing, capital markets (property sales and commercial mortgage origination), valuation, loan servicing and other portfolio services, for occupiers and investors worldwide.

revenue.note: FY2024 $7,729M; source FY2025 10-K segment note and MD&A

businessLines.revenueNote: FY2024 $7,729M; source FY2025 10-K segment note and MD&A

businessLines.name: Building Operations & Experience (BOE)
businessLines.how: Corporations and property owners sign multi-year contracts and pay monthly for CBRE to run their buildings; a large part of reported revenue (about 54%) is pass-through cost of subcontractors billed to the client at no markup, so the profit is a thin fee on top.
businessLines.description: Enterprise and local facilities management, property management, digital-infrastructure (data center) technical services, and flexible workplace through Industrious (fully owned since January 16, 2025). Segment created in 2025; formerly Global Workplace Solutions plus property management.

revenue.note: Includes $12,529M of pass-through costs (53.9% of segment revenue); pass-through was 55.3% of segment revenue in FY2024, FY2024 revenue not extracted

businessLines.revenueNote: Includes $12,529M of pass-through costs (53.9% of segment revenue); pass-through was 55.3% of segment revenue in FY2024, FY2024 revenue not extracted

businessLines.name: Project Management (Turner & Townsend)
businessLines.how: Clients (developers, corporates, governments) pay fees for managing capital projects, mostly fee-for-service; about 54% of segment revenue is reimbursable pass-through cost, so the fee is the margin.
businessLines.description: Program management, project management and cost consultancy for real estate, infrastructure and natural-resource projects, delivered through Turner & Townsend. CBRE owns 70% of the combined entity since January 2025.

businessLines.name: Real Estate Investments (REI)
businessLines.how: Institutional investors pay recurring management fees on assets managed, plus carried interest and incentive fees when funds outperform; development earns fees on built-to-suit work and gains when CBRE-owned or co-invested projects are sold (lumpy).
businessLines.description: Investment management (CBRE Investment Management, $155.5B assets under management at Dec 31, 2025) and real estate development (Trammell Crow Company, in-process portfolio and pipeline over $29.5B).

operatingProfit.note: FY2024 $261M. Includes $432M gain on disposition of real estate (FY2024 $142M) and $48M equity income that are not in revenue; also adds back a $132M Telford fire-safety provision and $44M wind-down costs.
